decisions.evidence: Round 2, entry 3 presentation offers a personal note “or…tags/labels”; entry 4 responds, “I’d want both: tags for organizing and a short personal note for context.”
decisions.note: Discovery-stage choice presented two individually incomplete alternatives; the client supplied the reference-conforming combination.

decisions.evidence: Round 2, entry 3 asks whether old links need “a saved copy” or only a note/title; entry 4 selects “an actual saved copy…For a PDF…the PDF itself preserved.”
decisions.note: The client selected the reference-conforming preservation alternative during discovery.

decisions.evidence: Round 4, entry 7 proposes a core flow of save, add context, and find; entry 8 approves only with “including what happens if I try to save a link that’s already there.”
decisions.note: The proposed core walkthrough omitted duplicate convergence, and the client added it.

decisions.evidence: Round 5, entry 9 presents pasting a URL and clicking “Save link”; entry 10 says, “Saving feels clear.”
decisions.note: Prototype-review decision conforms to URL-based saving.

decisions.evidence: Round 5, entry 9 presents automatic title and description only; entry 10 says, “I expected the app to collect the page’s icon and a preview image too.”
decisions.note: The initial metadata decision omitted two required automatically collected fields.

decisions.evidence: Round 5, entry 9 presents the saved list without a favicon; entry 10 requests showing “at least the icon in the saved list.”
decisions.note: The client added the required per-item favicon to the list presentation.

decisions.evidence: Round 5, entry 9 proposes “a simple comma-separated list”; entry 10 requests suggestions for existing tags such as “javascript” and “reference.”
decisions.note: Comma-separated entry lacked the required existing-tag autocomplete.

decisions.evidence: Round 5, entry 9 describes the note as a free line “to your future self”; entry 10 requests “a proper longer note with simple formatting.”
decisions.note: The client replaced the one-line note decision with a rendered Markdown-style note.

decisions.evidence: Round 5, entry 9 only exposes fields during saving; entry 10 says, “I’ll also need to be able to edit the link and all these details after saving.”
decisions.note: The client added post-save editing of the required bookmark fields.

decisions.evidence: Round 6, entry 11 presents automatic icon and preview collection and both in the list; entry 12 says both are useful and the list remains readable.
decisions.note: Revised prototype conforms to metadata collection and readability-first list exposure.

decisions.evidence: Round 6, entry 11 presents clickable, narrowing existing-tag suggestions; entry 12 says they work as expected.
decisions.note: Revised tag entry conforms to autocomplete.

decisions.evidence: Round 6, entry 11 presents only bold and bullet formatting; entry 12 asks that common Markdown such as links “render safely too.”
decisions.note: The client extended the initially limited Markdown rendering during prototype review.

decisions.evidence: Round 7, entry 13 presents search across title, description, note, address, and tags; entry 14 says those fields are what the client wants.
decisions.note: The required title, description, note, and URL full-text fields are covered; tag matching is additional.

decisions.evidence: Round 7, entry 13 presents live full-text search without specifying case behavior; entry 14 requires “Closure” and “closure” to return the same result.
decisions.note: The client added the required case-insensitive rule.

decisions.evidence: Round 7, entry 13 presents text entry as the finding interaction; entry 14 adds, “Clicking a displayed tag filters to that tag.”
decisions.note: The client added direct tag selection.

decisions.evidence: Round 7, entry 13 demonstrates ordinary words such as “reading”; entry 14 requires “Typing #reading searches the tag specifically.”
decisions.note: The presented search scope lacked the required #tag syntax.

decisions.evidence: Round 7, entry 13 presents ordinary substring search; entry 14 requires exact phrases in quotation marks.
decisions.note: The client added exact-phrase search.

decisions.evidence: Round 7, entry 13 presents basic live filtering; entry 14 adds AND/OR/NOT, parentheses, implicit word-plus-tag AND, and quoted operator words as literals.
decisions.note: The client supplied the missing structured-search grammar and literal-operator rule.

decisions.evidence: Round 8, entry 15 presents case-insensitive search, exact #tags, clickable tag filtering, phrases, Boolean groups, and quoted operator literals; entry 16 confirms the searches behave as expected. Round 11, entry 21 records that #tag is exact.
decisions.note: Linked clarification and later summary establish the revised search decision as conforming without double-counting the pending exact-tag detail.

decisions.evidence: Round 9, entry 17 makes “Show the one I already have” merely jump to and highlight the bookmark; entry 18 says it “should open that bookmark for editing.”
decisions.note: Highlight-only handling did not guide the user into editing the existing bookmark.

decisions.evidence: Round 9, entry 17 treats path capitalization differences as the same address; entry 18 explains that path capitalization can identify a different page and should not generally be normalized.
decisions.note: The duplicate identity rule incorrectly collapsed potentially distinct URLs.

decisions.evidence: Round 10, entry 19 opens an equivalent duplicate in a full edit form, updates it in place, preserves path case distinctions, and blocks edit collisions; entry 20 says this now feels right.
decisions.note: Revised duplicate and editing behavior conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 11, entry 21 calls the save/find/edit baseline complete without a main-item navigation action; entry 22 adds that selecting the title or main card should open the original page.
decisions.note: The client supplied the missing original-URL navigation behavior.

decisions.evidence: Round 15, entry 29 presents fully expanded long title, description, and note text that makes one card dominate, offering full versus shortened display; entry 30 chooses shortening with “Show more.”
decisions.note: The client selected the readability-first alternative.

decisions.evidence: Round 15, entry 29 presents one long scrolling list and asks whether it is acceptable; entry 30 rejects that and requires sorting by date and title.
decisions.note: The offered single-list behavior omitted required list sorting.

decisions.evidence: Round 16, entry 31 presents clamped list text with expansion and whole-result sorting by date/title; entry 32 says the behavior is exactly what was expected.
decisions.note: Revised large-list presentation conforms to readability and sorting requirements.

decisions.evidence: Round 17, entry 33 explicitly places “reading-status tracking” outside the proposed first build; entry 34 rejects implementation approval and requires unread/read controls and an unread-only view first.
decisions.note: Specification-gate deferral omitted central read-state requirements.

decisions.evidence: Round 17, entry 33 defers archiving; entry 34 requires archive/restore separately from permanent deletion before implementation.
decisions.note: Specification-gate correction restores archive, archive view, reversibility, and permanent delete distinctions.

decisions.evidence: Round 17, entry 33 defers saved page/PDF preservation; entry 34 says local page copies, actual PDF preservation, and optional Internet Archive submission must be settled first.
decisions.note: The proposed first build omitted both preservation requirements.

decisions.evidence: Round 17, entry 33 defers bulk actions; entry 34 requires selecting several links or all matching links for tag, read, archive, and delete actions.
decisions.note: The client restored both selected-item and all-current-filter bulk scopes.

decisions.evidence: Round 17, entry 33 leaves saved filters outside the build; entry 34 requires saving search plus included/excluded tags for reuse.
decisions.note: The proposed first build omitted bundles/saved filters.

decisions.evidence: Round 17, entry 33 defers import/export; entry 34 requires browser-bookmark import/export retaining titles, tags, and original dates.
decisions.note: The client restored both Netscape-style transfer requirements at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 17, entry 33 defers preferences; entry 34 requires default sort, displayed count, and text-size preferences before implementation.
decisions.note: The first-build scope omitted required display-related settings.

decisions.evidence: Round 18, entry 35 presents mark read/unread controls and All/Unread/Read filtering; entry 36 says the dot, button, and filter are clear.
decisions.note: The read-state prototype covers marking and separate unread viewing.

decisions.evidence: Round 18, entry 35 presents the read/unread flow without specifying filtered-view updates; entry 36 requires an item marked read in “Unread only” to disappear immediately.
decisions.note: The client added the required consistency between state change and unread-only results.

decisions.evidence: Round 19, entry 37 presents a default-checked “Read later” choice that can be unchecked to save as read; entry 38 confirms it matches the intended reading queue.
decisions.note: This provides a conforming way to set initial unread state.

decisions.evidence: Round 20, entry 39 presents reversible archive/restore, a separate Archived view, and confirmed permanent deletion; entry 40 says the model feels right.
decisions.note: Archive and delete are correctly distinguished.

decisions.evidence: Round 20, entry 39 presents the archive flow but does not specify ordinary-search scoping; entry 40 requires Active as default, archived items excluded from active list/search, and archive searches limited to archived items.
decisions.note: The client supplied the reference edge rule for archived-search isolation.

decisions.evidence: Round 21, entry 41 presents automatic private saved copies, actual PDF storage, retry after failed capture, and explicit optional Internet Archive submission; entry 42 confirms that split.
decisions.note: The principal preservation decisions conform.

decisions.evidence: Round 21, entry 41 offers capture-once versus later refresh/re-capture; entry 42 selects “Capture it once…don’t silently replace it later.”
decisions.note: The client selected preservation of the original snapshot rather than replacement.

decisions.evidence: Round 21, entry 41 describes a preserved page without specifying the required file form; entry 42 requires “a self-contained single HTML file.”
decisions.note: The client added the reference’s single-file HTML constraint.

decisions.evidence: Round 21, entry 41 does not state snapshot lifecycle under archive/delete; entry 42 requires archive to retain the saved copy and permanent delete to remove it.
decisions.note: The client supplied the required content-retention and permanent-removal lifecycle.

decisions.evidence: Round 22, entry 43 presents multi-selection, add/remove tags, read/unread, archive/restore, delete, and “Select all matching” over the complete filtered scope; entry 44 confirms the selection model.
decisions.note: Bulk actions and whole-filter application conform; the requested picker is a UI refinement, not a reference divergence.

decisions.evidence: Round 24, entry 47 presents reusable saved searches but does not state dynamic membership; entry 48 requires bookmarks to appear or disappear automatically as they begin or cease matching.
decisions.note: The client added the required dynamic bundle behavior.

decisions.evidence: Round 25, entry 49 limits “Words to match” to plain words; entry 50 replaces that limitation with full phrase, Boolean, and parentheses syntax under “Search terms.”
decisions.note: The saved filter’s search term was improperly weaker than the approved search language.

decisions.evidence: Round 26, entry 51 presents grouped full search syntax combined with include/exclude tag pickers; entry 52 says it now matches the client’s intent.
decisions.note: Revised bundle builder conforms to reusable dynamic search conditions.

decisions.evidence: Round 27, entry 53 presents browser-bookmark HTML import preserving titles, tags, and original dates; entry 54 confirms that format and mapping.
decisions.note: Import decision conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 27, entry 53 presents browser-compatible HTML export retaining titles, tags, and original dates; entry 54 confirms this is the desired export rather than a full backup.
decisions.note: Export decision conforms; excluding notes, state, and saved copies is not a reference divergence.

decisions.evidence: Round 28, entry 55 presents default sort, page size, and text size preferences, with built-app persistence explicitly distinguished from prototype reset; entry 56 settles those preferences.
decisions.note: The settings decision conforms to the reference fields.

decisions.evidence: Round 29, entry 57 limits the first build to “simple safe formatting” and records “richer Markdown in notes” for later; entry 58 gives general scope approval without identifying or explicitly accepting the Markdown shortfall.
decisions.note: At the specification gate, the presented Markdown subset departs from the unqualified rendered-Markdown requirement. Bare overall approval does not establish awareness or acceptance.

decisions.evidence: Round 29, entry 57 records the finalized save, metadata, tags, search, duplicate/edit, navigation, read state, sort, archive/delete, bulk, bundle, import/export, Internet Archive, and preference behaviors; entry 58 says the scope matches what was settled.
decisions.note: Final specification-gate decisions other than the separately classified Markdown and snapshot-fidelity issues conform to the reference.

decisions.evidence: Client entry 42 explicitly requires “a self-contained single HTML file.” At implementation review, round 30 entry 59 discloses that CSS/font inlining is only “best-effort”; entry 60 says, “The limitations you noted are understood” and accepts the application.
decisions.note: The client had explicitly stated the self-contained expectation and then accepted the disclosed implementation limitation. This is an accepted implementation-review divergence, not bare approval in isolation.
